title: FELA: A Multi-Agent Evolutionary System for Feature Engineering of Industrial Event Log Data

mechanism.domainTask: Evolutionary feature engineering for industrial event-log data
mechanism.populationDetail: Each idea is treated as an island containing associated feature implementations; the maintained hierarchy is concept/feature-centric rather than a conventional pool of executable programs.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate bounded elite archive is described; all generated features/code are accumulated and a best solution is selected from the accumulated sets.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Algorithm 1 appends newly evaluated features and code to F and C; idea-feature knowledge is updated, while best-so-far selection is not described as a distinct archive.
mechanism.generationDetail: Feature Proposer generates implementations conditioned on an existing idea, Idea Creator makes new ideas, and Idea Synthesizer explicitly combines existing ideas; these operate at concept/feature level rather than by editing a selected code parent.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The online search reward is relative AUC improvement; other reported metrics and critic rejection/correction feedback should not be mistaken for preference-based evaluation.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: UCB chooses an idea in the shared knowledge base for feature evolution; this is a concept-level trajectory choice rather than selection of an executable parent program. Idea synthesis takes existing ideas as sources, with no fixed parent count.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Evolution occurs over a hierarchical idea-feature knowledge base, with UCB selecting concept trajectories and memory distilling cross-trajectory feedback; this is not fully represented by candidate-program population and parent-selection labels.
